title: Welcome to BookSphere
author: BookSphere Team
text:
Chapter 1. Reading here

Every book on BookSphere is free to read. Open any book and it opens at the page where you stopped last time. Use the arrow keys or the Next and Prev buttons to turn pages.

Chapter 2. Highlighting

Select any words in this paragraph. A small bar appears with four colours. Pick one and the words stay highlighted every time you return. Click a highlight to remove it or add a note.

Chapter 3. Bookmarks and progress

Press the bookmark button to save a page. Your dashboard shows every book you are reading, the pages left in each, the books you want to read later and the books you have finished.

Chapter 4. Make it yours

Open the Aa tab to change the text size, font, spacing, width and theme. Use the speaker button to hear the page read aloud, and select a single word and press Define to see its meaning.

title: Fables for Quiet Evenings
author: After Aesop
text:
The Tortoise and the Hare

A hare laughed at a tortoise for walking so slowly. The tortoise smiled and challenged him to a race. The hare sprinted ahead, then lay down under a tree, sure he had time to spare.

The tortoise kept walking, one patient step after another. When the hare woke, the tortoise was already crossing the line. Slow and steady wins the race.

The Fox and the Grapes

A hungry fox saw ripe grapes hanging high on a vine. He jumped again and again but could not reach them. At last he walked away saying, They were probably sour anyway. It is easy to despise what we cannot have.

The Ant and the Grasshopper

All summer the grasshopper sang while the ant carried grain to his nest. When winter came, the grasshopper had nothing to eat and asked the ant for help. The ant replied, You sang in summer, so now you may dance in winter. Prepare today for the days to come.
